card: PR 36170 skips automatic Tor onion service creation when a node configures explicit -bind options without a dedicated -bind=<addr>=onion listener. Instead of forwarding incoming Tor connections to a normal P2P port where peers can mistakenly inherit IP-based whitelist permissions, the node logs a warning, skips incoming service registration, and preserves Tor control for outbound proxy discovery. Wildcard onion binds are rejected at startup when automatic onion listening is enabled, and the Tor controller startup is moved after socket binding so failures do not race service registration.
changed_since_previous: Instead of refusing startup when explicit -bind options lack an onion bind, the node now boots normally, skips automatic incoming onion service creation with a warning, and keeps Tor control active for outbound SOCKS proxy discovery. Starting the Tor controller is also deferred until after P2P listeners bind successfully.
evidence: Addresses open issue #33458, 'Documentation trap when using -bind in conjunction with (automatically configured) Tor hidden services'

PR description: 'With a normal -bind (but no dedicated onion bind), automatic Tor services can forward incoming connections to the normal P2P listener, where they may be misclassified and inherit IP-based whitelist permissions.'
problem: When explicit -bind options are configured without a dedicated =onion listener, automatic Tor service creation forwards incoming Tor connections to a standard P2P listening port. The node cannot distinguish these from local or clearnet connections, misclassifying Tor peers and potentially granting them IP-based whitelist permissions applied to the Tor daemon. Additionally, starting Tor control before socket binding can register an onion service before discovering that local port binding failed.

risk.why: Mistakes in listener and Tor controller initialization could break inbound or outbound Tor connectivity or prevent the node from starting.

summary: Skip automatic Tor onion service creation when explicit -bind arguments lack a dedicated =onion bind, while keeping the Tor controller running for outbound proxy discovery. Reject wildcard onion binds at startup when automatic onion listening is enabled, and defer starting the Tor controller until listening sockets have bound successfully.
